common_dose_finding.what_the_scopes_found: As found, Umatilla Electric Coop Assn (19325:OR) at capped_at_25_points, capped_at_50_points has a common capped change under rule 8.1's own histories and none under the place test's wider set, where an admissible history is a counterexample (each scope's reason is in verdicts_by_scope). Under Joe's ruling the wider set governs and the exclusion is retained there. Every other form of these utilities has the same verdict under both scopes.
common_dose_finding.rule: Joe, D-105: a common change in capped dose established from complete admissible histories is applied for that capped form; otherwise exclusion is retained and what remains unestablished is stated. Joe, D-107: the complete admissible histories are the wider set, not narrowed to obtain settled status. The uncapped form takes no exception (the agent's reading of 'for the capped form'): it enters only if its histories here give one common change, and they do not for either utility.

definitions.change_in_dose: the load share in points, counted at no more than the cap in each year, averaged over 2023-2025 less the same averaged over 2008-2010 (rule 8.1)
definitions.classified_at: each form at its own cap: uncapped, capped at 25 points, capped at 50 points (D-105)
definitions.class_2: no data center load above zero in any year of 2008-2010 or 2023-2025 in any modeled history; what it establishes is no endpoint exposure in modeled histories, not a verified absence of sites (D-46 ruling 6)
definitions.settled_before_apparent_zero: class 4 is tested before class 6; a class 4 utility that is zero as assigned and above zero in some history keeps the flag not_a_verified_zero
definitions.settled_is_conditional: "Settled" (class 4) is conditional on rule 8.1's modeled histories with dates held at their conventions: a settled utility is settled within those histories, and its dose was not tested against the admissible range of any site's date (Joe, D-107, 2026-11-19; the wording is the session's)
definitions.not_settled: classes 5 to 8 only, for leverage reporting; class 2's share is reported on its own line
definitions.two_point_line: applied at each form to that form's change; a convention chosen before any range was computed

runs.as_assigned: every utility with a dose as assigned, the same at every form
runs.settled_only_classes_2_to_4: classes 2, 3 and 4 at that form, each at its dose as assigned
runs.ten_highest_leverage_not_settled_left_ou: every utility with a single dose at that form less the ten highest-leverage among classes 5 to 8 at that form, ranked by leverage at that form among every utility with a single dose there (adopted by Joe on 2026-11-19, D-111)
runs.per_form_members: each form's run uses the members its own cap's classes give (adopted by Joe on 2026-11-19, D-111)

definitions.sample: every panel unit usable in all six years with a market region in each and residential customers in 2010, less the price hold. Crypto-mining load and the simulation's access list are not grounds the plan gives for leaving a unit out of the second number, and none is applied

as_built_case_against_the_dose_file.what: the as-built case of assignment.matrices over the 2009-2011 base against utility_year_dose.dose, in points, every unit with a dose row that no load-unknown site reaches

enumeration_against_the_as_built_case.what: pass_c_exact._State.grid at the reference configuration (screen shift 0) against the as-built case, every unit of the state that no load-unknown site reaches

left_out_before_the_frame.9094:AL: price hold (price_hold.csv): on neither side of any design

analysis_eligibility_apart_from_simulati.statement: The simulation's access list (pipeline/analysis/simulation_access_list.*) decides nothing about who is in the second number's sample. The sample is every panel unit usable in all six years with a market region and a size band, less the price hold (build_frame, _sample_candidates); neither takes the access list, and this count is the only place the module reads it. Every unit counted here stays in the sample.
analysis_eligibility_apart_from_simulati.how: power_simulation.design at 2% with history_settled(0.02), restrict_to_access_list, unknown.gate at 2%

sensitivity_scenarios.status: adopted by Joe on 2026-11-19 (D-107); built and summarized apart
sensitivity_scenarios.what: Joe adopted the two whole-inventory histories of D-106 R2 on 2026-11-19 (D-107), including their early-end settings for the two sites with no load history, and asked that they be described as sensitivity scenarios, not bounds or necessarily one-change comparisons with the primary analysis, with the sample differences reported. Scenario A places every unresolved load-carrying site at its runner-up under the inventory's own placement rule; scenario B puts each date entry in force that has a convention at the other end of its interval. In both, bi:852-0 starts in 2024, bi:837-0's date and the rest of its capacity are at 2011, and each state's factor is recomputed. Built in pipeline/analysis/second_number_scenarios.py; the quantity-side summary is data/frozen/second_number_scenarios.json.

limitation_check.statement: The only whole-inventory assignment it builds is the inventory as assigned (pipeline/facilities/build_inventory.py).
limitation_check.what_the_code_does: build_inventory.main builds one facilities frame: one serving utility per site (pick_utilities, then overrides and step D's assignment corrections), one date and one capacity per site, one state factor per state (state_anchor at 2024). Nothing in it enumerates another assignment. pass_c_expand.scratch_state rebuilds a scenario for one state at a time, with assignment held at the corrections, so it is not a whole-inventory assignment either.

limitation_check.statement: D-46 ruling 4's cases (assignment.py, CASES and matrices) are each utility's own extremes and, by that module's own description, cannot all be true at once.
limitation_check.what_the_code_does: matrices returns utility-by-year GWh for every utility in the lower and upper cases (as built and with no anchoring) and for the inventory as built. In the upper matrix an unresolved site is added to every candidate at once, and in the lower matrix it is on no one; the module docstring says a site that is a candidate for two utilities is counted on each in its own upper case, which cannot both be true. The as-built case reads the inventory's factor; no factor is recomputed, which is right for a move of assignment alone (the anchoring does not depend on who serves a site). It supplies loads by year, so each utility's within-case endpoint doses can be read from it; it does not supply a joint inventory.

limitation_check.statement: The verification pass's state scenarios all_earliest and all_latest (pass_c_expand.py) are joint within a state for date and capacity questions only, hold assignment at the map, and are not ordered by dose.
limitation_check.what_the_code_does: run_state adds all_earliest ({q: EARLY for every date and capacity question in the state}) and all_latest; scratch_state applies them to one state with assignment corrections as given and otherwise as mapped. That an earlier start can raise the 2008-2010 endpoint as well as the later one follows from the ramp (buildout.ramp_mw is non-increasing in the start year in every year), so neither scenario orders a change in dose. Note: run_state runs on the inventory the pass's corrections are written against (load_frozen), not on the step D rebuild.

limitation_check.statement: The place test's enumeration (pipeline/facilities/timing.py) runs over each utility's dependency component and records places and crossings, not endpoint doses.
limitation_check.accurate: accurate as to what it records, with one qualification
limitation_check.what_the_code_does: StateRun.evaluate records places, crossings, ranges of crossings and verdicts. The pure function it evaluates with, pass_c_exact._State.grid, returns the utility's GWh in every panel year, as built (factor recomputed per configuration) and with no anchoring, for every configuration of the questions relevant to that utility. So within-history endpoint doses for ONE utility can be read from it (this module does so for the two load-unknown utilities), but each configuration is of that utility's relevant questions only, every other question at the reference: it is not a whole-inventory scenario.

limitation_check.statement: The second number's simulation (power_simulation.run_second_number) reads doses as assigned only and leaves out every utility a load-unknown site reaches.
limitation_check.what_the_code_does: run_second_number drops every unit in unknown_load.affected from the comparison pool and from the dose frame before building D0 from the dose file (the inventory as assigned), and names them as carried to step F.
